title: Reassessing Dataset Quality and Fine-Tuning Practices for Vulnerability Detection on PrimeVul dataset
abstract: arXiv:2611.06373v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recent studies report promising results from supervised fine-tuning of pre-trained code language models for automated vulnerability detection on benchmarks such as PrimeVul. In this paper, we present a large-scale empirical evaluation of both model performance and dataset quality in this setting.   We systematically fine-tune three widely used encoder models (CodeBERT, GraphCodeBERT, and UniXCoder) across five imbalance mitigation strategies, extensive hyperparameter sweeps, and multiple random seeds, resulting in 770 independent training runs.   Our results reveal a consistent pattern. While standard metrics such as F1 and ROC-AUC occasionally suggest improvements, security-critical and calibration-aware measures tell a different story. Matthews Correlation Coefficient remains near zero, predicted probabilities are poorly calibrated, and evaluation under strict false-positive constraints reveals high false-negative rates. translated_title: 重新评估PrimeVul数据集上漏洞检测的数据集质量与微调实践
translated_abstract: 近期的研究报告显示，在PrimeVul等基准数据集上对预训练代码语言模型进行有监督微调以实现自动化漏洞检测取得了可喜的成果。本文对这一场景下的模型性能和数据集质量进行了大规模的实证评估。我们系统地微调了三种广泛使用的编码器模型（CodeBERT、GraphCodeBERT和UniXCoder），涵盖五种类别不平衡缓解策略、广泛的超参数搜索以及多个随机种子，共进行了770次独立训练。我们的结果揭示了一个一致的模式：虽然F1和ROC-AUC等标准指标偶尔显示出改进，但安全关键型和校准感知型指标却呈现出截然不同的景象。马修斯相关系数（MCC）始终接近于零，预测概率校准效果不佳，且在严格假阳性约束下的评估显示出很高的假阴性率。无论是类别不平衡（原文摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文通过对770次训练的大规模实证评估发现，在PrimeVul数据集上微调的代码语言模型虽然在F1和ROC-AUC等标准指标上看似有改进，但在安全关键指标上（MCC接近零、概率校准差、严格假阳性约束下假阴性率高）实际漏洞检测能力远低于表面评估结果。
en_tdlr: Through a large-scale empirical evaluation of 770 training runs on PrimeVul, this paper reveals that while fine-tuned code language models appear to improve on standard metrics like F1 and ROC-AUC, security-critical measures (near-zero MCC, poor calibration, and high false-negative rates under strict false-positive constraints) show their real vulnerability detection capability falls far short of surface-level evaluation results.
